title: Pull a crept rail back so both joints are at the 10 mm expansion gap
instruction: The middle length of the near rail has crept: its left joint is shut and its right joint is wide open. Set both joints to the 10 mm expansion gap. Stand the yellow 10 mm shim upright in the right joint against the fixed rail end and hold it there, slide the middle length to the right until it bears on the shim, let go of the rail, then lift the shim out, put it back on the table where it started, in front of the sleeper ends, and move both grippers away.
context: Track maintenance workers keep jointed rail at its expansion gaps (O*NET 47-4061.00, Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators, and track labourers). Traffic and braking make rails creep along the track, shutting some joints and opening others. A shut joint cannot take up summer expansion and the track can buckle; an open one batters the rail ends and breaks joint bars. The fix is to pull the rail back: with the fastenings slackened, one worker holds a shim as thick as the rail-temperature table gives in the joint while another draws the rail up to it, and the shim is taken out. An 18 m rail changes length by about 0.21 mm per deg C, so rail laid at -5 deg C needs about 10 mm. The middle length here sits between two fixed rails, so opening one joint closes the other, and both joints are checked with a taper gauge: a free part slid onto a held gauge, two coupled gaps read.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. 'Left' and 'right' are the robot's own. A bench-scale length of jointed track runs along y; every box is square to the table; 15 objects, nothing else on the table. (1) Sleepers: four fixed dark-brown painted hardwood bars, 260 mm along x, 25 mm along y and 18 mm tall, from x 16.0 to 42.0 cm, centred at y +25.0, +8.0, -8.0 and -25.0 cm. (2) Near rail (the one nearer the arms), two fixed lengths: steel-grey painted aluminium bars 20 mm wide (x), 25 mm tall and 235 mm long on the outer sleepers, from x 21.0 to 23.0 cm, one from y +16.5 to +40.0 cm and one from y -16.5 to -40.0 cm; their inner end faces are 330 mm apart. (3) Middle length: a loose steel-grey painted aluminium box section (4 mm walls), 20 mm wide, 25 mm tall, 310 mm long, 0.25 kg, lying on the two middle sleepers from x 21.0 to 23.0 cm with its centre at y +1.0 cm: its ends are at y +16.5 and -14.5 cm, so the left joint is shut (0 mm) and the right joint 20 mm, which leaves the 10 mm shim 5 mm clear of each rail end. (4) Rail seat shoulders: four fixed dark-grey painted aluminium blocks, 6 mm (x) by 25 mm (y) by 10 mm tall, on the middle sleepers either side of the middle length, centred at x 20.2 and 23.8 cm and y +8.0 and -8.0 cm; their inner faces, at x 20.5 and 23.5 cm, leave the rail 5 mm of play each side, so it can turn at most 3.1 degrees. (5) Far rail: fixed steel-grey painted aluminium bars, 20 mm wide and 25 mm tall, from x 35.0 to 37.0 cm: two 235 mm lengths from y +16.5 to +40.0 cm and from y -16.5 to -40.0 cm, and a 310 mm length centred at y 0, leaving correct 10 mm joints at y +16.0 and -16.0 cm. (6) Expansion shim: a loose yellow-painted steel plate, 60 mm (x) by 10 mm (y) by 45 mm tall, 0.21 kg, standing on its 60 x 10 mm edge on the table centred at x 12.0 cm, y -16.0 cm (x 9.0 to 15.0 cm), in front of the sleepers' near ends, its 60 mm side across the track. Every rail top is 43 mm above the table; standing on the table, the shim's top is 2 mm above the rail tops.
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz) from the poses of the middle length and the shim and each gripper's finger-tip point (between its finger tips). Left gap: 165 mm minus the largest y of any corner of the middle length; right gap: the smallest y of any corner plus 165 mm. Each is the joint's narrowest point, as a taper gauge reads it; square, the two add up to 20 mm. 'Seated': the middle length's lowest corner is 16 to 20 mm above the table (the sleeper tops are at 18), its 25 mm axis is within 3 degrees of vertical (either way up), and its centre line crosses y +8.0 and -8.0 cm within 6 mm of x 22.0 cm (between its shoulders). 'Shim in the right joint': its lowest corner within 3 mm of the table top, part of it at x 21.0 to 23.0 cm (across the rail's line) and its centre between y -16.5 cm (the fixed rail end's face) and the middle length's right end. 'On the track': some corner of the shim at x 16.0 to 42.0 cm, |y| below 42.0 cm and lower than 45 mm above the table (2 mm above the rail tops). 'Put away': the shim's lowest corner within 3 mm of the table top and every corner at x below 16.0 cm (in front of the sleeper ends), standing or lying. 'Hands off': each finger-tip point at least 60 mm from the middle length and from the shim. 'Still': over the last 0.5 s (10 control steps) the centres of both parts each moved along a path shorter than 2 mm. 'Gauged', a record kept for the whole trial: on some step the shim was in the right joint within 1 mm of both the fixed rail end and the middle length (outline to outline) while the right gap was 8.5 to 11.5 mm, so the joint was set on the gauge. Score, checked in this order: 0 if the middle length is not seated or either gap is under 3 mm; 0.25 if the shim is in the right joint, held or let go (a joint with the gauge left in cannot close); 0 if the shim is anywhere else on the track (on a rail or a sleeper, between the rails, in the left joint, poking in between the sleepers); 1.0 if both gaps are 8.5 to 11.5 mm, the shim is put away, hands are off, both parts are still and 'gauged' was set; 0.5 if both gaps are 6 to 14 mm (for example a gripper still on a part, the shim held or put down off the track but not in front of it, a part moving, or the joints set by eye without the gauge); 0.25 otherwise (both gaps at least 3 mm, one under 6). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Every outcome falls in exactly one. Seated and square, with the shim put away, hands off, both parts still and 'gauged' set, as the left gap goes from 0 to 20 mm the score is 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0, changing at a left gap of 3, 6, 8.5, 11.5, 14 and 17 mm (the start, 0 mm, scores 0). The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. Real trial: a taper gauge in each joint at its narrowest point; a top photo showing the middle length between its shoulders on both middle sleepers, the shim on the table in front of the sleeper ends and both grippers at least 6 cm from both parts; and, from the video, whether the shim stood in the right joint against the fixed rail end with the middle length's end on it.
fidelity: Bench scale: the rails are 20 x 25 mm aluminium bars and the middle length is 310 mm, not 18 m; the 10 mm gaps are full size. No fishplates, bolts or clips: the rail is taken as unclipped, kept in line by fixed shoulders with 5 mm play. On real track the shim stays in until the joint is bolted; here it comes out once the rail is let go. Uniform simulator friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), so the bar drags more than a rail on its plates. No thermal model: the target gap is given.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the middle length back on the two middle sleepers between its shoulders, its centre 10 mm left of the track's centre: its left end against the fixed rail end (left joint shut) and its right joint 20 mm (checked with feeler gauges). Stand the shim on its 60 x 10 mm edge on the table centred at x 12.0 cm, y -16.0 cm, its 60 mm side across the track.
